title: Make, let, help, get
intro: Some verbs take a person and then a verb without “to”: make someone do something, let someone do something. “Help” works with or without “to”. “Get” needs “to”. Hindi thinking often adds “to” after make and let, which sounds wrong in English.

rules.rule: make + person + base form (force or cause).
examples: My boss made me stay late.
My parents let me travel alone.

rules.rule: help + person + (to) verb. get + person + to verb.
examples: I got him to fix it.

mistakes.wrong: I got him fix my laptop.
mistakes.right: I got him to fix my laptop.

ex.q: The teacher made us ___ the essay again.
I got my brother ___ me to the airport.
Can you help me ___ this box?
My father didn't let me to go.
ex.fixed: My father didn't let me go.

ex.q: The news made her to smile.
Let us discuss about the plan.

ex.a: Please let me know if you need anything.

talk: Talk about your childhood: what your parents let you do, what they made you do, and who helped you learn something important.
